analysis.title: Iran: Peak Gamma
key_insights: Frank Flight (Citadel Securities Head of Macro Strategy) frames Iran's decision-making as being long a high-strike oil call that expires around the US midterms. The framework is an analytical device, and the note acknowledges it abstracts from the human consequences of the conflict.
Iran's leverage has risen as the conflict has persisted and oil has moved higher. Polling suggests gasoline prices are politically consequential for the White House.
The value of Tehran's leverage may be greater before the midterms than after them.
Oil is still near local highs but shows signs of upside exhaustion, with only a few weeks left until the midterms. The note argues Tehran is approaching peak gamma.

Near the strike and close to expiry, small moves in the underlying produce large changes in delta. That leaves Iran with a highly convex position while time decay accelerates and shortens the window for converting disruption to Hormuz into political pressure.

Carrying the optionality into expiry gets more costly because gamma and time decay are both elevated near the strike. An option holder may choose to monetise ahead of expiry rather than keep exposure to a binary terminal payoff.
The note's conclusion is that reopening Hormuz in exchange for an end to the war could let Tehran convert temporary, highly convex leverage into a more durable political outcome.
risk_factors: Oil price weakness or upside exhaustion would reduce Iran's leverage ahead of the midterms.
Passage of the midterms without a deal would remove the political value of Iran's Hormuz leverage.
Tehran may carry the position into expiry rather than monetise it early.
vol_and_positioning: Framework treats Iran's position as a long high-strike oil call near expiry: gamma is elevated, theta decay is accelerating, and the position is highly convex.
geopolitical: Iran conflict with the US, with Tehran's leverage tied to disruption of the Strait of Hormuz
Possible reopening of Hormuz in exchange for an end to the war
US midterm elections as the political deadline, with gasoline prices a pressure point for the White House

tension_points.bull_case: Iran's leverage is at its highest because oil is near local highs and gasoline prices carry political weight for the White House ahead of the midterms.
tension_points.bear_case: Oil shows signs of upside exhaustion and time decay is accelerating, so the leverage loses value as the midterms approach and pass.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The midterms passing without a Hormuz-for-peace deal, which removes the political value of the leverage.

theme_stances.key_argument: Iran is approaching peak gamma, so reopening Hormuz in exchange for an end to the war could lock in a durable political outcome.
